beats.beat: Garret, Elin, and Dessa saddle up to chase the caravan, with Dessa guiding them along a shortcut she knows from the trading route.
Elin worries aloud that even catching the caravan won't help, since the painted veins look convincing to anyone without Garret's eye.
Elin remembers something no one has ever tested: a true mature leaf stays faintly warm against a breath, while an unripe one stays cold, and she tries it on a leaf from Jasper's rack.
The test confirms the leaf is unripe, and they reach the crossing at Tollgate just as the caravan driver is handing the bundles over to Kettering's buyer.
beats.note: Buyer is described only as 'a man in a buyer's grey coat,' not named as Kettering's, but the context carries it.

turn.note: Elin's demand to stop the exchange with her own test, not Garret's word, sets up chapter 5's public proof scene.

continuity: Garret says 'they'll say the old cutter from Earlmere is talking down another man's crop to raise the price of his own. It has been said before,' asserting a prior accusation against him that no earlier chapter established; it reads as a reason presented as already known rather than built on anything the story has shown.

problems: The attribution 'said Elin, riding up level with him' is placed as its own narrator segment splitting one speech across three segments awkwardly.

listenability: Opening sentence 'They were out of Earlmere on three horses' leans on a pronoun for a trio only fully named one sentence later.

generic_prose.quote: which frightened her more than the hurry did
generic_prose.replace_with: show a concrete physical detail of her fright, e.g. her hands tight on the reins, rather than naming the feeling

trope_note: Serves all three declared tropes directly: Elin's apprentice initiative, the silver-vein rule under test, and the untested breath-warmth property finally proven; no fourth trope introduced.
fixes: Open with the three riders named outright: 'Garret, Elin, and Dessa were out of Earlmere on three horses before the mist had come off the millpond.'
Cut or ground 'It has been said before' — either remove the claim of a prior accusation or plant it earlier in the series of chapters so it isn't asserted cold.
Merge 'said Elin, riding up level with him' into the surrounding Elin dialogue rather than giving it its own narrator segment.
Trim 'which frightened her more than the hurry did' to a concrete physical beat instead of a named feeling.

The chapter runs well over its 450-word target; tighten the opening paragraph and the ford-arrival paragraph, both of which restate established texture (drying leaves, cart road) rather than advancing the beat.

findings.quote: The mist across the glass thinned and was gone before she had counted three, and the vein ran silver under it, and the leaf was warm against...
findings.note: 3 clauses coordinated in 29 words. Heard once, the last one lands with the subject of the first already gone. Split after the first clause, or make every member the same grammatical shape so the ear can follow the pattern.
